name: cut-paper-stop-motion
title: Cut-paper stop-motion
summary: Flat printed paper cut-outs with wobbly hand-cut edges and soft contact shadows on a mottled ground, posed 15 times a second under a perfectly smooth camera.

look.ground: a printed paper backdrop: vertical gradient, two scales of mottling, faint print lines, dust, a warm key light falling to darker corners

palette.where: the one thing that matters: the subject, its prop
small lights: windows, clouds, letters, steam
smallest details: birds, legs, hair, foreground leaves

look.type: Archivo Black capitals cut as paper sprites that drop and boil like everything else; or a clean sans on a quiet band
look.texture: paper fibre on every piece (soft-light, 0.45-0.55), print lines at 5-8 % on fabric and facades, grain re-rolled per pose
look.light: one warm key from the top left; a cream rim on edges that face it; contact shadows offset down-right in world space at 0.3
look.materials: flat printed paper; shades mix toward the ink or the cream, never toward black or white

consistency: characters are rigs of flat parts on pivots (a cut coat, capsule limbs, a head on a neck pivot), baked once and reused in every shot

moves: poses at 15 a second: floor(15t)/15, two frames each at 30 fps
camera push 1 to 1.08-1.14 over a shot, every frame
crouch before a jump, squash 0.82 on landing, one pose each
replacement drawings for wings, never a rotated wing

pace.text: under 30 s: one scene whose state changes on each phrase; a handoff object crosses each cut in a relay

banned: shading toward pure black or white
12 poses a second at 30 fps (uneven holds stutter)
source: the cut-paper recipes in an open MIT skill (klsoen/opus-js-animations, references/styles.md); no reference clip, so pace is the recipe's, not measured
